answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of compute-proof-work per identity to protect the network from sybil-based erosion. The verifier enforces this by checking if each hash output is as clear as a crystal, confirming energy was spent on a unique task rather than replay. An honest agent pays this base cost for one entry, but a malicious actor attempting to spawn 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, flying toward the ledger like a falcon into a gale. This tide of computational debt prevents cheap roots; fraud triggers a permanent burn, assuming compute cannot be pooled.
